subject: Science
title: Plants around us
objectives: Children will name trees, flowers and leaves and say that plants are alive.
Children will explore the school garden with their senses.
content: Naming trees, flowers, leaves and grass, noticing that plants are alive, and exploring the school garden with the senses.
teachingActivities: Use real plants from the compound; let children touch, smell and look; name parts such as leaf, flower and trunk; link to the plants children know such as mango, pawpaw and hibiscus.
learnerActivities: Name a tree, a flower and a leaf and say that plants are alive and grow.
resources: Real leaves, flowers and a small potted plant
Pictures of a mango tree, a hibiscus, grass and a palm
assessment: Observe whether each child names a tree, a flower and a leaf and says that plants grow.
expectedOutcomes: Names a tree, a flower and a leaf.

lessons.title: Trees and flowers
lessons.subject: Science
objectives: Children will name trees and flowers and say that plants are alive.
successCriteria: Names a tree and a flower
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can name animals, babies and small creatures and have been in the garden.
resources: Pictures of a mango tree and a hibiscus
lessons.starter: Show a potted plant and say "This plant is alive. It needs water and sun to grow."
teacherActivities: Show the tree and flower pictures and name them.
Touch the potted plant and talk about its parts.
Say "Plants are alive. They grow." and show growth with your hands.
Go outside and find a tree and a flower.
learnerActivities: Children look and say the names.
Children touch the leaf and stem gently.
Children grow tall like a plant.
Child points to a tree and a flower.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Show the tree and flower pictures and name them. Children: Children look and say the names.
Step 2. Teacher: Touch the potted plant and talk about its parts. Children: Children touch the leaf and stem gently.
Step 3. Teacher: Say "Plants are alive. They grow." and show growth with your hands. Children: Children grow tall like a plant.
Step 4. Teacher: Go outside and find a tree and a flower. Children: Child points to a tree and a flower.

practical.title: Plant walk
steps: Walk to the garden in a line.
Find a tree and a flower.
Touch the leaves gently and name them.
practical.safety: Check the garden for thorns, poisonous plants and insects first. Remind children not to pick plants or eat any part.

differentiation.support: Point to the plant and say the name together.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to find two different plants.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

expectedOutcomes: Names a tree and a flower
lessons.conclusion: Stretch up tall like a tree and then sit down.
lessons.homeConnection: Name trees and flowers on the way home.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "name trees and flowers and say that plants are alive" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

learnerFacing.songOrRhyme: A seed grows into a plant. Grow, grow, grow.

lessons.title: Leaves and grass
lessons.subject: Science
objectives: Children will look closely at leaves and grass and describe them.
successCriteria: Says a word for the colour or shape
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can name animals, babies and small creatures and have been in the garden.
resources: A patch of grass or a tray of grass
lessons.starter: Hold up a leaf and say "This is a leaf. It is green." Ask "What colour is it?"
teacherActivities: Pass leaves round and let children touch them.
Look closely at a leaf with a magnifying glass and point out the lines.
Touch the grass and say "The grass is green and soft."
Make a leaf rubbing with paper and a crayon.
learnerActivities: Children touch and say leaf.
Children look and point.
Children touch the grass and say green.
Child rubs a crayon over a leaf under paper.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Pass leaves round and let children touch them. Children: Children touch and say leaf.
Step 2. Teacher: Look closely at a leaf with a magnifying glass and point out the lines. Children: Children look and point.
Step 3. Teacher: Touch the grass and say "The grass is green and soft." Children: Children touch the grass and say green.
Step 4. Teacher: Make a leaf rubbing with paper and a crayon. Children: Child rubs a crayon over a leaf under paper.

practical.title: Leaf rubbing
steps: Put a leaf under a sheet of paper.
Rub a crayon gently over it.
practical.safety: Use leaves from safe plants only and wash hands afterwards. Do not allow leaves to go in mouths.

differentiation.support: Rub the crayon together and look at the pattern.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to make three rubbings and compare the shapes.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

lessons.conclusion: Put the leaves back in the basket and wash hands.
lessons.homeConnection: Collect safe leaves with your child and look at their shapes.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "look closely at leaves and grass and describe them" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: Our school garden
lessons.subject: Science
objectives: Children will explore the school garden using their senses.
successCriteria: Looks, touches or smells a plant safely
Says one thing about the garden
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can name animals, babies and small creatures and have been in the garden.
lessons.starter: Say "Today we visit our garden. We use our eyes, nose and hands gently."
teacherActivities: Walk to the garden in a line and sit together.
Ask "What do you see?" and "What do you smell?"
Touch leaves gently and smell flowers safely.
Talk about what plants need: water, sun and soil.
learnerActivities: Children sit and look.
Child says a word or points.
Child touches and smells.
Children say water, sun or soil.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Walk to the garden in a line and sit together. Children: Children sit and look.
Step 2. Teacher: Ask "What do you see?" and "What do you smell?" Children: Child says a word or points.
Step 3. Teacher: Touch leaves gently and smell flowers safely. Children: Child touches and smells.
Step 4. Teacher: Talk about what plants need: water, sun and soil. Children: Children say water, sun or soil.

practical.title: Garden senses
steps: Walk to the garden in a line.
Use eyes, nose and hands to explore.
practical.safety: Check the garden for thorns, ants and poisonous plants beforehand. Do not allow children to pick or eat plants and wash hands afterwards.

differentiation.support: Explore beside the child and name what they touch.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to tell a friend what plants need.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

lessons.conclusion: Wave goodbye to the garden and wash hands.
lessons.homeConnection: Visit a garden or a farm with your child and talk about what you see.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "explore the school garden using their senses" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: Plant parts
lessons.subject: Science
objectives: Children will name parts of a plant: leaf, flower, stem and root.
successCriteria: Points to the leaf, the flower and the stem
Names at least two plant parts
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can name animals, babies and small creatures and have been in the garden.
resources: A real plant with roots washed clean
lessons.starter: Hold a plant and say "A plant has parts. Here is a leaf. Here is a flower."
teacherActivities: Point to each part on the plant and say its name.
Show the root and say "The root is under the soil."
Say a part and ask children to find it on the plant.
Match the part cards to the plant picture.
learnerActivities: Children point to the same part.
Children look and point down.
Child points to the part.
Child places a card on the picture.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Point to each part on the plant and say its name. Children: Children point to the same part.
Step 2. Teacher: Show the root and say "The root is under the soil." Children: Children look and point down.
Step 3. Teacher: Say a part and ask children to find it on the plant. Children: Child points to the part.
Step 4. Teacher: Match the part cards to the plant picture. Children: Child places a card on the picture.

practical.title: Plant parts
steps: Match the part cards to the picture.
practical.safety: Wash roots clean before handling and wash hands afterwards. Do not allow plant parts in mouths.

differentiation.support: Point to the part together and say its name.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to say what each part does.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

expectedOutcomes: Points to leaf, flower and stem
lessons.conclusion: Put the plant back and say "Thank you, plant."
lessons.homeConnection: Look at a plant at home and name its parts.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "name parts of a plant: leaf, flower, stem and root" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: Week 5 plants check
lessons.subject: Science
objectives: Teachers will observe how each child names plants and plant parts.
successCriteria: Names a tree, a flower and a leaf
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can name animals, babies and small creatures and have been in the garden.
lessons.starter: Sing the plant song and show three stations.
teacherActivities: Set up three stations: leaves, flowers and plant parts.
At each station ask "What is this?" and "Does it grow?"
Record each child’s level and take photographs.
learnerActivities: Children rotate every four minutes.
Child answers with a word or gesture.
Children wash hands and tidy.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Set up three stations: leaves, flowers and plant parts. Children: Children rotate every four minutes.
Step 2. Teacher: At each station ask "What is this?" and "Does it grow?" Children: Child answers with a word or gesture.
Step 3. Teacher: Record each child’s level and take photographs. Children: Children wash hands and tidy.

practical.title: Plant stations
practical.safety: Supervise each station and keep floors clear. Use safe plants and wash hands after.

differentiation.support: Provide an adult partner and use two plants.
differentiation.extension: Ask a confident child to name three plant parts.

assessment.method: Observe and record Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding for: names a tree, a flower and a leaf; says that plants grow; names plant parts.

expectedOutcomes: Has an observation record for Week 5
lessons.homeConnection: Talk about plants during walks and at mealtimes.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "Teachers will observe how each child names plants and plant parts" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?
